lines.text: Three animals that can actually talk to humans.
First, Koshik the elephant. For years, his only friends at a South Korean zoo were humans.
So he learned to speak their language.
By sticking his trunk in his mouth, he can say five Korean words, like hello, sit down, and no.
Next, the honeyguide. This bird teams up with humans to find honey.
When honey hunters in Africa call out brrr-hm, it flies over and leads them straight to a wild beehive.
That call more than triples their chances of finding one.
The humans take the honey, and the bird gets the wax.
Finally, Noc the beluga whale. In 1984, Navy divers kept hearing what sounded like people talking underwater.
Then one diver came up and asked, who told me to get out?
Nobody had. It was Noc, copying human voices.
